releases.summary: The page builder opens pages whose card grids or post lists set a number of columns, instead of stopping with an application error.
Content imports reach the server whole: the admin API no longer passes through the middleware, whose copy of the body could lose the uploaded file behind nginx.
Uploads (content and WordPress imports, media, form files, CVs) are recognised as files whatever class carried them, and an import that arrives without its file says what did arrive.
Forms can follow a design: no optional marker, an arrow on the send button, compact choice chips and the space inside the card. A card form follows the site's card corners.
The edge-to-edge hero keeps its proportions: the whole picture at full height, a least height, and the text stopping at a reading measure on wide screens.
An edge-to-edge hero picture can take a chosen share of the width, and the text beside it widens to match.

A card set to rounded corners stays rounded when the site's cards are cut, the contents column beside an article is no longer narrowed by the page padding, and the blog search row shows its label once.

Heading and text sizes for tablets and phones per section, the contained FAQ following cut corners, panel content lined up with the page, the blog's category bar on category pages with the search on its own row, and an edge-to-edge hero that fills the space beside the notch header.
Colours for every form field and unchosen choice chip, forms that run the full width of their section, and cover pictures on the plain post cards.

The footer can show the uploaded logo and be drawn as a panel; a split hero can run its picture to the section's edges; buttons can each have an arrow or not; the line under each section can be switched off, and section headings can run wider.

A successful update no longer ends with a false 'Command failed: pm2 reload' — the reload is read from the version the restarted site reports. The release list is held to the limits every site checks.

A new major version gathering everything since 2.12, plus glitch text on headings (noise, psycho, split — optional, per block), the platform's credits in two meta tags and in Settings, and the engine's own name throughout. Admins sign in once more after updating.
Every Read more comes from Site translations, the media band's fade starts from the site's accent, and the notch header's clearance follows the header height setting.

Picture rows and mixed-width rows for the card grid, glowing and ruled stats, check lists on circles and in cards, a line beside a form's button, a category index block, blog search in the category bar and a featured post, and round “Read more” arrows.

Cut corners for cards, buttons, fields, chips, pictures and sections; sections as inset panels; a notch header with its own link typography; button glow, font and arrow compartment; a dot marker for section labels; a side-fading media band; Chakra Petch.

Content imports are checked row by row like the editor's saves, can merge instead of replacing, and report what they did as a CSV. A WordPress importer reads an export file or a live site, maps types and taxonomies, cleans page-builder shortcodes, downloads media and adds redirects. Appearance gains a Motion screen with a reduce-motion switch for everyone.

A menu-button header, glass or see-through headers that hide or shrink on scroll, an overlay menu with pictures, a custom pointer, page transitions, a preloader, side rails and a reveal footer. Pages and sections can use their own colours; blocks hide per screen size and columns reorder; cards tilt; reviews take logos, roles and companies; galleries hold 200 pictures with load more.

Posts can have a share bar, a contents column that follows the reader, previous/next, related posts by category and an author box; archives gain a categories menu, breadcrumbs, card options, category pictures, blocks around the posts and RSS feeds. Share pictures, structured data and titles work, the 404 page can be any page, and social links gain 13 networks.

Video that plays on iPhones (byte ranges), moving pictures that loop silently while on screen, a film behind any section, SVG uploads cleaned of anything that could run, and responsive picture sizes with AVIF — each off until you switch it on.

Integrations for tracking tags, with a content policy built from what is switched on; a real cookie-consent manager with Google Consent Mode v2; CAPTCHA on every public form; and forms that email their answers, reply to the visitor, open a thank-you page, track conversions, carry campaign fields, ask questions conditionally and feed webhooks.
Saved blocks: design a block once and use it anywhere — synced everywhere, or pasted as a template. Duplicate pages, posts, projects, saved blocks and popups. Copy and paste blocks between pages.

Projects: a portfolio built from blocks, with categories, tags, archive pages and a shared page template. A Projects block can fill itself from them — featured, by category, with load-more or real pages. Project addresses join Permalinks.

The blog's addresses are a setting — under the blog, under a category or at the top level, with a trailing-slash option and 301s from the old addresses. Archives page on the server (/blog/page/2/). Posts can show their blocks. Redirects gain prefixes, patterns, query rules and CSV import and export.

A converging diagram can have more than two sources — add a label, get a box and a curve. And its colours, text sizes, line thickness and corner radius can be changed. Three labels still draws exactly what you have today.

A hero draws the converging diagram from its own labels, separately from the figure block. 2.11.1 fixed one and not the other, so editing the wrong one changed nothing. Both now show the words on the page, and a converge diagram stops offering a fourth label it cannot draw.
The words in a diagram can be edited. The figure block’s label list started empty while the page drew “SOURCE A”, so there was no box containing what was on screen and the diagram looked locked.

Space between items and animation speed are now settings — site-wide under Appearance, and per block in its Design tab. Left empty, every block keeps what it was drawn with, so nothing changes until you ask it to.

Status and chart colours, and the text sizes inside blocks, are now yours to change — with the values that were already compiled in as the defaults, so nothing moves. The words inside blocks can be translated at last.

A card grid now has a Space between cards field — a different thing from a card’s own margin, which only shifts that card inside its cell. Left empty, each layout keeps the spacing it was designed with.

Cards can be styled one at a time — background, text colour, spacing, border, radius, alignment — on every card layout. And a heading with its subtitle beside it can line the two halves up at the top, centred or at the bottom instead of always centring them.

npm run release:merge now finishes after a conflict. It told you to merge by hand and run it again, then stopped because there was nothing left to merge — so it never checked or tagged. Only relevant to sites kept in their own repository.

Line breaks you type in Body, Intro and Description fields now appear on the page. They were being collapsed, so text ran together with nothing in the editor to say so. Fixed for every block rather than one at a time.

Fixes the test suite failing in the public repository. The licence test added in 2.6.1 read files that repository does not carry, so it was red over a licence that was correct. A guard now stops a test shipping that cannot pass where it lands.

The engine is now MIT licensed. It was published with no licence at all, which legally meant all rights reserved. The bundled typefaces keep their own licences, which the notice states rather than glossing over.

Typography size, weight, colour and letter spacing now show the block’s real values — and stay silent where a section’s headings genuinely differ, rather than naming one of them. Measured against your saved theme rather than the shipped defaults.

Background colour, border widths, border colour and corner radius now show the block’s real values instead of “inherit” — and the fields that genuinely inherit nothing, like an overlay or a gradient stop, now say none.

Fixes the block spacing added in 2.2.0, which never appeared: the browser was refusing to load the page the panel measures, and a refusal looks exactly like a feature that does not work. The Design tab now shows each block’s real padding and margin.

One command — npm run release:merge — takes a release into a site that has changes of its own, and refuses to tag anything it cannot verify: a conflicted merge, a wrong version, or a merge that quietly replaced a file you had changed.

Updating is safer. An update now proves the release is the version it claims, and refuses to check one out over commits your own site has — your ports, your process name — instead of replacing them and reporting success. Release tags can no longer collide with your own.

A block’s Design tab now shows the spacing it already has, per screen size, instead of leaving you to guess what a value would replace. Measured from the block itself rather than read from a list, so it stays true as blocks change.

Fixes an update that finished but could never say so. The reload restarts the process writing the record, so the panel sat on “reload…” for ever and refused every later update. It now settles such a run from the version actually running, and always offers a way to clear one.

Write your own CSS — for the whole site, or for one page — and switch on Google Analytics with a measurement id. Saving a page now shows the change straight away: three caches were holding the old one, and there is a Clear cache button for when one still does.

Fixes updating: the update now finds your site’s process instead of assuming it is called “engine”, stops on a failed migration instead of rebuilding anyway, and adds npm run db:status. No database changes.

Your site can speak more than one language, advertise jobs and take applications. Fifty-five more typefaces, including Armenian. What visitors send is now deleted after a period rather than kept for ever.
Export a site's content — pages, posts, media and design — and import it into another site. No accounts and no visitor data travel with it.
Three more roles — manager, author and reviewer — alongside administrator and editor. Existing accounts are unchanged.
The first release: block builder, templates, sliders, forms, popups, email, security, backups, and a browser installer that writes its own configuration.
